allowed_dependency_manifest.content: For each fixed integer n greater than 1, consider the function E_n(x) = floor(n x) minus the sum over integers k with 1 <= k <= n of floor(k x) divided by k. The task is to determine the set of real x values for which E_n(x) attains its maximum over all real x, and to determine the corresponding maximal value M(n).

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer n with n > 1 and every integer a with 0 <= a <= n-1, the inequality E_n(a divided by n) <= H_n minus 1 holds. Moreover, E_n(a divided by n) equals H_n minus 1 if and only if a equals n minus 1.

payload.statement_nl: For every integer n>1 and every integer a with 0 <= a <= n-1, one has E_n(a/n) <= H_n - 1, and equality holds if and only if a = n-1.

result_payload.proof_nl: Let H_n = sum_{j=1}^n 1/j and {t} = t - floor(t). For x = a/n with integer a, floor(nx) = a, so E_n(a/n) = a - sum_{k=1}^n floor(ak/n)/k = sum_{k=1}^n {ak/n}/k, since floor(ak/n) = ak/n - {ak/n}. If a = 0, then E_n(0) = 0 < H_n - 1, so assume 1 <= a <= n - 1. Write d = gcd(a,n), n = dm, a = d alpha with gcd(alpha,m) = 1. For k = qm + r with 0 <= q <= d - 1 and 1 <= r <= m, we have {ak/n} = {alpha r / m}; in particular, it is 0 when r = m. For 1 <= r <= m - 1 define rho_r in {1,...,m - 1} by rho_r ≡ alpha r (mod m). Because alpha is invertible modulo m, the numbers rho_r are a permutation of 1,...,m - 1. Hence E_n(a/n) = (1/m) sum_{r=1}^{m-1} rho_r S_r, where S_r = sum_{q=0}^{d-1} 1/(qm+r). The sequence S_r is strictly decreasing in r. Now compare permutations: if i < j but rho_i < rho_j, swapping rho_i and rho_j changes the sum by (rho_j - rho_i)(S_i - S_j) > 0. Therefore the maximum over all permutations rho_r is attained when rho_1 > rho_2 > ... > rho_{m-1}, i.e. when rho_r = m - r. So E_n(a/n) <= (1/m) sum_{r=1}^{m-1} (m-r) S_r = sum_{r=1}^{m-1} sum_{q=0}^{d-1} (m-r)/(m(qm+r)). For each q,r we have dm - (qm + r) = (d-q)m - r >= m - r, so (m-r)/(m(qm+r)) <= (dm-(qm+r))/(dm(qm+r)) = (n-k)/(nk), with k = qm + r. Therefore E_n(a/n) <= sum_{k=1}^{n-1} (n-k)/(nk) = sum_{k=1}^{n-1}(1/k - 1/n) = H_n - 1. This proves the inequality. For equality: if a = n - 1, then d = 1, m = n, alpha = n - 1, and rho_r = n - r, so every step above is an equality and E_n((n-1)/n) = H_n - 1. Conversely, if equality holds, then the last comparison must be an equality, which forces d = 1, because if d > 1 then the omitted multiples of m contribute positive terms to H_n - 1. Thus m = n and S_r = 1/r. Equality in the swap argument then forces rho_1 > rho_2 > ... > rho_{n-1}, so rho_r = n - r for all r. In particular rho_1 = a = n - 1. Hence equality holds iff a = n - 1.
result_payload.proof_summary: Express E_n(a/n) as a weighted sum of fractional parts. After factoring out gcd(a,n), the fractional parts form a permutation with decreasing weights, so a swap/rearrangement argument gives the reverse-order maximum. A termwise comparison with (n-k)/(nk) yields H_n-1, and equality forces a=n-1.
